_comment: Job scanner config TEMPLATE. Copy to user-library/scanner_config.json and fill in your own criteria during onboarding. TWO source kinds: (1) discovery_sources = BROAD market discovery across keyless remote-job aggregators (surfaces roles at companies you never pre-listed); (2) an OPTIONAL per-company ATS watchlist ('always also check these'). The 'criteria' block is the shared scoring/filtering brain. EVERYTHING below is an EXAMPLE with sensible defaults — the tier/keyword/watchlist lists are examples, NOT a fixed whitelist; trim or extend freely. No personal data is baked into the script; it all lives here.
_browser_pass_note: BROWSER-PASS SOURCES (LinkedIn, Wellfound, Built In) are NOT configured here — they run as a manual browser pass in the scheduled task and are saved as fetched/{source}__{label}.json files. Built In (builtin.com) is a tech/startup board: include it when your field is tech; skip it for non-tech. URL patterns: national-remote = https://builtin.com/jobs/remote/<category>?search=<role>; metro = https://builtin.com/jobs/<region>/<category>?search=<role> (region slugs: colorado, nyc, chicago, los-angeles, seattle, austin, boston, san-francisco, washington-dc). Save to fetched/builtin__<label>.json and/or fetched/builtin-<region>__<label>.json. All builtin* files are picked up automatically by the scanner.

remotive._note: https://remotive.com/api/remote-jobs?search=<query>. One fetch per query. Free-text search is loose, so the role-title regex does the real precision work downstream.

remoteok._note: https://remoteok.com/api — single endpoint, no query param. Returns the latest ~100 jobs across all categories; the role-title regex filters to your roles.

arbeitnow._note: https://www.arbeitnow.com/api/job-board-api — single endpoint. Europe-heavy; most rows drop on the US-location gate, but it occasionally surfaces remote-US startup roles.

jobicy._note: https://jobicy.com/api/v2/remote-jobs?count=<count>&tag=<tag>. One fetch per tag. Remote-only board.

adzuna._note: OPTIONAL. Needs a free Adzuna API key (app_id + app_key from developer.adzuna.com). When enabled AND keys are set, queries the US jobs endpoint with max_days_old. When disabled, skipped silently. Adzuna salaries are often PREDICTED estimates, not employer-stated — the script ignores predicted figures so they can't trip the sub-floor drop.

_watchlist_comment: OPTIONAL supplement — specific company boards to ALSO check on top of broad discovery. Set watchlist_enabled=true to use it. ats is greenhouse|lever|ashby; token is the board slug in the API URL (Ashby tokens are CASE-SENSITIVE). Verify a token resolves before trusting it (e.g. curl 'https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/TOKEN/jobs?content=false'). These three are EXAMPLES ONLY — replace with companies you care about.

watchlist.note: REPLACE - example only: a real Greenhouse board slug
REPLACE - example only: a real Ashby board slug (case-sensitive)
REPLACE - example only: a real Lever board slug

criteria._comment: The scoring/filtering brain. role_title_regex (if set) is the precise title gate; role_keywords/levels are the simpler fallback. levels are listed MOST-PREFERRED FIRST. locations are acceptable location substrings; home_terms get the top location score. Comp is annual USD. Replace every REPLACE with your own search.
criteria.role_title_regex: REPLACE-OPTIONAL - a precise title gate, e.g. (senior|staff|principal|lead|director).*(product design|design)|(product )?design (lead|manager)|head of (product )?design
criteria._role_title_regex_note: OPTIONAL. When set, this regex is the role-title gate (more precise than role_keywords). When empty/removed, the scanner falls back to role_keywords (+levels if require_level is true). Leave the REPLACE string and it simply won't compile to anything useful — set a real regex or delete the key to use the fallback.
criteria._require_remote_or_home_note: When true, drops roles that are neither remote/worldwide NOR in your home_terms (i.e. onsite-elsewhere). Leave false to keep any US-acceptable location.
criteria._max_age_note: RECENCY GATE. Drops postings older than this many days ONLY for sources that expose a post/updated date (remoteok, remotive, jobicy, greenhouse, lever, ashby, arbeitnow, adzuna). Rows where the source gives NO parseable date are KEPT (benefit of the doubt, same as unknown-comp rows). Set to 0 or null to disable. Robust to messy/missing date formats: a bad date is treated as 'no date' and the row is kept.
criteria._comp_note: comp_target = the number that earns full comp points; comp_floor = the number below which an EXPLICITLY-listed sub-floor role is DROPPED. Unknown-comp rows are always KEPT (they just get no comp boost). Set both to 0 to ignore comp entirely. Defaults assume annual USD (see accept_currencies / comp_band below to scan in another currency).
criteria._currency_note: NON-US USERS set these. accept_currencies = currency codes/symbols a salary must be in to be trusted as comp (a figure in any other currency is ignored, never mis-ranked as USD). comp_band = [min, max] plausible ANNUAL figure in that currency, so an hourly/monthly number isn't mistaken for salary — widen it for high-denomination currencies (e.g. INR/JPY). Leave as ["USD"] + [40000, 1000000] for a US search.
criteria._allow_unleveled_note: When true, a bare role title with NO level word (e.g. plain 'Product Designer') still passes the role gate IF it lists comp_max >= comp_floor (comp acts as the seniority proxy). Bare-title roles with unknown or sub-floor comp are dropped. Leveled roles always pass regardless of comp. Requires a real comp_floor to be useful.
criteria._signal_note: Generic role-fit signals, +8 each (cap 30). Use these for skills/themes that make a role a good fit but aren't the role's SHAPE or DOMAIN.
shape_signals: REPLACE - add YOUR role's shape phrases, e.g. design: 'first design hire' / 'founding designer' / 'sole designer'; eng: 'founding engineer' / 'first backend hire'; PM: 'first PM' / 'founding product manager'; sales: 'first sales hire' / 'founding AE'; nursing: 'charge nurse' / 'unit lead'
criteria._shape_note: ROLE-SHAPE handling — works for ANY profession. shape_signals describe a role's SHAPE independent of domain (founding / first-hire / 0->1 / team-of-one / generalist breadth). The entries above are role-NEUTRAL and already generalize; the REPLACE line is where you add the phrases specific to YOUR field (design: 'first design hire'; engineering: 'founding engineer'; PM: 'first product manager'; marketing/sales: 'first sales hire', etc.) — onboarding should rewrite that slot to your role and remove this instruction string. Each card-text hit is worth shape_signal_points (14, vs 8 for a generic signal), capped at shape_signal_cap (24). SEPARATELY, shape_baseline_points (12) is added to ANY role whose shape is your sweet spot — a leveled IC, in an acceptable location, with comp not sub-floor (unknown comp gets benefit of the doubt) — even with NO shape_signal text and NO domain match. That baseline is the 'thin-card but right-shape' deep-read trigger: a browser card with a thin description still surfaces on level+location+comp alone, where the full JD makes the real call. Set shape_baseline_points to 0 to disable the baseline. Downweighted manager-only roles never get the baseline (it is IC-shaped only).
tier1_keywords: REPLACE - your top-priority domains, e.g. travel, design tool, creator tool, no-code
tier2_keywords: REPLACE - your nice-to-have domains, e.g. climate, developer tools, personal finance
bonus_keywords: REPLACE - optional extra mission keywords you care about
criteria._tier_note: DOMAIN IS NON-EXHAUSTIVE / BENEFIT-OF-THE-DOUBT. The tier lists are a curated BONUS, not a gate: a Tier-1 match adds +18, a Tier-2 (or bonus) match adds +9, and NO match is NEUTRAL (no penalty). An unlisted domain is NEVER on its own a reason to keep a strong-fit role under the deep-read bar — only exclude_keywords actually drop a domain. Keep these lists short and meaningful; you don't need to enumerate every acceptable domain.
exclude_keywords: REPLACE - hard-no domains, e.g. crypto, gambling, defense
criteria._exclude_note: The ONLY domain hard-no. Any posting whose title/description/company contains one of these is DROPPED before scoring. This is the one place a domain can disqualify a role; everything else is non-exhaustive bonus.
criteria._manager_note: Manager/Head-of/Director titles are downweighted (-12) UNLESS one of these player/coach cues is present (signaling the role still does hands-on IC design). Manager-only roles never get the IC right-shape baseline.
criteria._deep_read_note: TWO-STAGE SCORING. Stage 1 = the cheap card/listing-level score this script computes for EVERY discovered role — enough to rule out the ~half that are obvious comp or domain mismatches. Stage 2 (done by the AGENT, not this script) = for any role whose card score is GREATER THAN deep_read_threshold (50), open and fetch the FULL JD, extract real comp + scope, do a live-status check, and re-score before recommending. Do NOT deep-read everything — only the cards already promising enough to be worth the closer look. The shortlist marks each item deep_read=true/false on this threshold. Raise it to deep-read fewer cards; lower it to deep-read more borderline ones.
